title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Enforcement Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1: If an applicant for enforcement applies for enforcement to the People's Court at the location of the property to be executed, it shall provide evidentiary materials proving that there is property available for enforcement within the jurisdiction of that People's Court.

Article 2: For an enforcement case over which two or more People's Courts have jurisdiction, if a People's Court, before filing the case, discovers that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already filed the case, it shall not file a duplicate case.
If it discovers after filing the case that another People's Court with jurisdiction has already filed the case, it shall revoke the case; if enforcement measures have already been taken, it shall deliver the controlled property to the enforcement court that first filed the case for handling.

Article 3: After a People's Court accepts an application for enforcement, if a party raises an objection to jurisdiction, it shall do so within ten days from the date of receipt of the notice of enforcement.
The People's Court shall review the objection raised by the party. If the objection is upheld, it shall revoke the enforcement case and notify the party to apply for enforcement to the People's Court with jurisdiction; if the objection is not upheld, it shall rule to reject it. If a party is not satisfied with the ruling, it may apply to the next higher People's Court for reconsideration.
During the period of review and reconsideration of the jurisdictional objection, enforcement shall not be suspended.

Article 4: For a case in which a People's Court has taken property preservation measures, if the applicant for enforcement applies for enforcement to another People's Court with jurisdiction other than the People's Court that took the preservation measures, the People's Court that took the preservation measures shall deliver the preserved property to the enforcement court for handling.

Article 5: During the enforcement process, if a party or an interested person considers that the enforcement act of the enforcement court violates legal provisions, it may raise an objection in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law.
The enforcement court shall review and handle the enforcement objection and shall make a ruling within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the written objection.
Article 6: If a party or an interested person applies for reconsideration in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall do so in writing.

Article 7: The written materials for a party or an interested person's application for reconsideration may be submitted through the enforcement court, or may be submitted directly to the next higher People's Court of the enforcement court.
After receiving the application for reconsideration, the enforcement court shall, within five days, submit the case file materials required for reconsideration to the next higher People's Court; after receiving the application for reconsideration, the next higher People's Court shall notify the enforcement court to submit the case file materials required for reconsideration within five days.

Article 8: If a party or an interested person applies for reconsideration in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, the next higher People's Court shall complete the review within thirty days from the date of receipt of the application for reconsideration and make a ruling. If there are special circumstances requiring an extension, with the approval of the president of that court, the period may be extended, but the extended period shall not exceed thirty days.

Article 9: During the period of review and reconsideration of the enforcement objection, enforcement shall not be suspended.
If the person subject to execution or an interested person provides sufficient and effective security and requests the suspension of the corresponding disposition measures, the People's Court may permit it; if the applicant for enforcement provides sufficient and effective security and requests continued enforcement, enforcement shall continue.

Article 11: If the next higher People's Court, in accordance with Article 226 of the Civil Procedure Law, orders the enforcement court to enforce within a time limit, it shall issue an enforcement supervision order to the enforcement court and notify the applicant for enforcement in writing of the relevant circumstances.
If the next higher People's Court decides to enforce the case by itself or directs another People's Court within its jurisdiction to enforce it, it shall make a ruling, serve it on the parties, and notify the relevant People's Courts.

Article 12: Where the next higher People's Court orders the enforcement court to enforce within a time limit, and the enforcement court, without justifiable reasons, still fails to complete enforcement within the specified period, the next higher People's Court shall rule that the case be enforced by itself or direct another People's Court within its jurisdiction to enforce it.

Article 13: The six-month period provided in Article 226 of the Civil Procedure Law shall not include the period of announcement, the period of expert evaluation and appraisal, the period for handling jurisdictional disputes, the period for coordinating enforcement disputes, the period of suspension of enforcement, and the period of discontinuance of enforcement.

Article 14: If a person other than a party claims ownership of the subject matter of enforcement or has other substantive rights sufficient to prevent the transfer or delivery of the subject matter of enforcement, it may, in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, raise an objection to the enforcement court.

Article 15: During the period of review of the objection of a person other than a party, the People's Court shall not dispose of the subject matter of enforcement.
If a person other than a party provides sufficient and effective security to the People's Court and requests the lifting of the sealing-up, seizure, or freezing of the subject matter of the objection, the People's Court may permit it; if the applicant for enforcement provides sufficient and effective security and requests continued enforcement, enforcement shall continue.
If the lifting of the sealing-up, seizure, or freezing due to the provision of security by the person other than a party is erroneous, causing the subject matter to be unable to be enforced, the People's Court may directly enforce the secured property; if the provision of security by the applicant for enforcement to request continued enforcement is erroneous and causes losses to the other party, compensation shall be made.

Article 16: During the trial of a lawsuit filed by a person other than a party regarding an enforcement objection, the People's Court shall not dispose of the subject matter of enforcement. If the applicant for enforcement requests the People's Court to continue enforcement and provides corresponding security, the People's Court may permit it.
If a person other than a party requests the lifting of the sealing-up, seizure, or freezing, or the applicant for enforcement requests continued enforcement erroneously, causing losses to the other party, compensation shall be made.

Article 17: Where multiple creditors apply for enforcement against the same person subject to execution or apply to participate in the distribution of the enforcement property, the enforcement court shall formulate a property distribution plan and serve it on each creditor and the person subject to execution. If a creditor or the person subject to execution has an objection to the distribution plan, it shall raise a written objection to the enforcement court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the distribution plan.

Article 18: If a creditor or the person subject to execution raises a written objection to the distribution plan, the enforcement court shall notify the creditors or the person subject to execution who did not raise an objection.
If the creditors or the person subject to execution who did not raise an objection fail to raise a contrary opinion within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, the enforcement court shall, after reviewing and amending the distribution plan in accordance with the objector's opinion, make distribution; if a contrary opinion is raised, the objector shall be notified. The objector may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, initiate an action in the enforcement court against the creditor or the person subject to execution who raised the contrary opinion as defendant; if the objector fails to initiate the action upon expiry of the time limit, the enforcement court shall make distribution according to the original distribution plan.
If distribution is made during the litigation period, the enforcement court shall deposit the amount corresponding to the disputed debt.

Article 19: If, within the last six months of the limitation period for application for enforcement, an applicant is unable to exercise its right of claim due to force majeure or other obstacles, the limitation period for application for enforcement shall be suspended. The limitation period for application for enforcement shall continue from the date on which the cause of the suspension is eliminated.

Article 20: The limitation period for application for enforcement shall be interrupted by application for enforcement, the conclusion of a settlement agreement between the parties, a demand for performance made by one party, or the consent to perform obligations by one party. From the time of the interruption, the limitation period for application for enforcement shall be recomputed.

Article 21: If an effective legal instrument provides that the debtor bears an obligation to refrain from acting, the limitation period for application for enforcement shall be calculated from the date on which the debtor violates the obligation to refrain from acting.

Article 22: If an enforcement officer takes compulsory execution measures immediately in accordance with Article 240 of the Civil Procedure Law, the notice of enforcement may be served simultaneously or within three days from the date of taking the compulsory execution measures.

Article 23: Where a person subject to execution is restricted from leaving the country in accordance with Article 255 of the Civil Procedure Law, the applicant for enforcement shall submit a written application to the enforcement court; when necessary, the enforcement court may decide on its own authority.

Article 24: If the person subject to execution is an entity, its legal representative, principal person in charge, or directly responsible personnel who affect the performance of the debt may be restricted from leaving the country.
If the person subject to execution is a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, its statutory agent may be restricted from leaving the country.

Article 25: During the period of restriction on leaving the country, if the person subject to execution performs all the debts determined by the legal instrument, the enforcement court shall promptly lift the restriction on leaving the country; if the person subject to execution provides sufficient and effective security or the applicant for enforcement consents, the restriction on leaving the country may be lifted.

Article 26: In accordance with Article 255 of the Civil Procedure Law, the enforcement court may, on its own authority or upon the application of the applicant for enforcement, publish the information that the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations determined by the legal instrument through media such as newspapers, radio, television, and the Internet.
The relevant expenses for publication in the media shall be borne by the person subject to execution; if the applicant for enforcement applies for publication in the media, the applicant shall advance the relevant expenses.

Article 27: If any judicial interpretation previously issued by this Court before the coming into force of this Interpretation is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
